title: Finneas, Other Acts Quit Ed Sheeran Tour After Macklemore Ousted Over Palestine
excerpt: Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Sheeran's own touring band Beoga walked out on Tuesday, accusing stadium owners led by Robert Kraft of silencing the rapper's onstage "Free Palestine" remarks.
body:
• Rapper Macklemore was dropped from the final eight US dates of Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour after telling a MetLife Stadium crowd "Free Palestine" on September 4.
  • Promoter Messina Touring Group said venue owners refused to stage concerts with Macklemore on the bill, .
  • Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Sheeran's touring band Beoga all quit the tour on Tuesday in protest.
  • Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez called Robert Kraft's role in lining up stadium owners an "abuse of power."

Macklemore announced on Instagram on September 14 that he had been removed from the remaining US dates of Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour after venue owners objected to his onstage support for Palestinians. A day later, every other act walked out in solidarity — leaving one of the year's biggest tours without an opener.

Macklemore removed after 'Free Palestine' shows

Macklemore, a longtime friend and collaborator of Sheeran's, opened the fall US dates with two nights at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Wearing a black-and-white keffiyeh, he told the September 4 crowd: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place, was so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine." He also performed "Hind's Hall," his 2024 protest track about Gaza. He had been slated for eight of the tour's ten remaining US concerts.

Messina Touring Group, the promoter behind the US leg, told Rolling Stone it had "been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans."

How stadium owners forced the call

The central figure in Macklemore's account is Robert Kraft, the billionaire New England Patriots owner whose company owns Gillette Stadium — booked for Sheeran shows on September 25 and 26. Macklemore said Sheeran told him Kraft had "rallied some of the other stadium owners" with an ultimatum: keep the rapper on the bill, and the venues would not host the concerts.

Kraft confirmed he barred Macklemore from Gillette, citing the rapper's onstage material and "a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery," including a 2014 costume widely read as an antisemitic caricature, for which Macklemore apologized. Kraft did not address the claim that he organized other venue owners. The ouster followed a September 7 petition from the Israeli-American Council.

Macklemore called Sheeran "a brother" and said the two had "difficult conversations." When Sheeran told him "Free Palestine" was "hurtful to a lot of people," he replied that "if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect."

"The stage becomes resistance. Maybe that's why this time it became so important to silence me."

— Macklemore

Four acts walk out in protest

On Tuesday, September 15, hours after Sheeran posted that the decision "was not mine," the rest of the lineup quit. Finneas O'Connell — the Grammy-winning producer, Billie Eilish's brother, booked for six South American dates in November and December — withdrew on Instagram.

"Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed. I stand with Palestine and its people."

— Finneas, singer and producer

Aaron Rowe, the Irish singer-songwriter, wrote: "as Irish people, we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation. I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up." Danish band Lukas Graham and Beoga, the Irish folk group that has long served as Sheeran's touring band, also left. The Wall Street Journal notes the departing acts were the only support performers listed on the tour's website.

Sheeran said in a six-slide Instagram statement that "Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter's decision, it was not mine" — the rapper's contract "was with the promoter, not me" — adding that while he respected Macklemore's "strength of purpose," he does not use his "professional platform for politics."

Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez called Kraft's actions an "abuse of power," warning that a handful of stadium owners could now jeopardize an artist's career over speech.

What's next

The Loop Tour resumes September 19 in Philadelphia with no opening acts listed. It has ranked No. 1 on global touring charts, with ten February shows grossing $70.8 million on 526,000 tickets, per Billboard. Some fans have demanded refunds, though standard policies say all sales are final and lineups can change. Whether Sheeran can restaff the bill will decide how the year ends.

For Indian-diaspora readers, the fallout is another reminder of how sharply pro-Palestinian speech is policed on Western pop's biggest stages.
